noticias.titulo: 3803 reproducciones · 43 reacciones | Vaccines protect people at every stage of life: from a child’s first days through adulthood and beyond. In early childhood, immune systems are still developing, leaving young children more vulnerable to serious illness. That’s why most routine vaccines are given in the first two years of life, offering protection when it matters most. As children grow into their teenage years, booster doses help keep that protection strong and respond to new and emerging health risks. During pregnancy, vaccination plays a crucial role in protecting both parent and baby. Recommended vaccines help pass protective antibodies to babies before birth, giving them a safer start in life. In adulthood and older age, the immune system naturally becomes less robust. Vaccines help reduce the risk of severe illness and hospitalization, helping people stay healthy and live longer. Vaccination is about care, prevention and giving every generation the chance to learn, grow and thrive. #VaccinesWork | World Health Organization (WHO)

Firefighters responded to 185 wildfires in the first 10 days of August. In coastal Suffolk, conservationists and locals are counting the cost of the blaze that devastated Dunwich Heath . Its vegetation and rare bird…

noticias.resumen: Te explicamos el fenómeno que provocó el terremoto magnitud 7,4 que sacudió el occidente de Colombia.

noticias.resumen: Netanyahu agradece la postura tomada por De la Espriella, mientras que países como Egipto y Arabia Saudí aseguran que la decisión viola el derecho internacional

noticias.titulo: Human rights groups sue Trump administration over ‘crippling’ ICC sanctions
noticias.resumen: Lawsuit challenges executive order targeting international criminal court for investigating Israeli crimes in Palestine Four prominent US human rights organizations have accused the Trump administration of using its “crippling” sanctions regime against the international criminal court (ICC) to undermine global efforts to prosecute war crimes and crimes against humanity. In a lawsuit filed in federal court on Tuesday, the groups – the American Friends Service Committee, the Center for Constitutional Rights, Human Rights Watch and the Open Society Institute – argued that the administration’s…

noticias.titulo: Los mapas y gráficos que muestran la magnitud y el impacto del potente terremoto en Colombia
noticias.resumen: Colombia se ubica sobre la zona de interacción de tres placas tectónicas. Es una de las naciones con mayor actividad sísmica de América Latina y ha sido escenario de potentes terremotos como el de este lunes.

noticias.titulo: France bans unsolicited telemarketing calls
noticias.resumen: Cold calling is coming to an end in France, with one consumer group calling the ban a "small revolution".

noticias.titulo: Dogs can tell fear from sadness — and scientists saw it in their brains
noticias.resumen: Dogs may understand our emotions more deeply than scientists realized. Brain scans show that happy human faces activate regions in dogs linked to higher-level processing and reward, suggesting that smiles carry special emotional significance for them.

noticias.titulo: Canadian airline cancels flight after child refuses to wear seatbelt
noticias.resumen: Flight from Victoria to Toronto forced to return to terminal after repeated attempts to secure child in seat failed A Canadian airline cancelled a flight from Victoria to Toronto after a child refused to wear a seatbelt. The child was standing in their chair as the 6 August Porter Airlines flight taxied towards the runway, the airline said. Repeated attempts by an accompanying parent and crew to secure the child in their seat failed, so the crew elected to return to the terminal and have the two passengers disembark as “the aircraft could not take off in this unsafe condition”, it added…

noticias.titulo: Milton Friedman, economista: "No existe un almuerzo gratis"
noticias.resumen: El economista Milton Friedman impulsó el monetarismo y fue uno de los mayores defensores de limitar la intervención estatal en la economía. Leer

noticias.titulo: MIT neuroscientists discover the brain can reason without words
noticias.resumen: MIT neuroscientists have found striking evidence that language and logical reasoning are powered by separate systems in the brain. Even people with severe language impairments caused by stroke were able to solve challenging logic puzzles as well as people without those impairments, while brain scans showed that language-processing regions stayed largely quiet during reasoning tasks.

noticias.titulo: “Cannot be explained” – New super steel stuns scientists
noticias.resumen: Scientists have created an unusually corrosion-resistant stainless steel that could replace costly titanium components used to produce green hydrogen. The breakthrough could reduce structural material costs by roughly 40 times and make seawater-based hydrogen production far more economical.

noticias.titulo: AI agent hacks gym to get its user a spot in pilates class
noticias.resumen: The incident is being seen as the latest example of the AI tools going to any lengths to complete their tasks.

noticias.titulo: Marine heatwaves are harming human health in surprising ways
noticias.resumen: Marine heatwaves are emerging as a threat not just to coral reefs and fisheries, but to human health and well-being. Researchers warn that unusually hot oceans can fuel stronger storms, trigger harmful algal blooms, reduce seafood supplies, disrupt livelihoods, and contribute to anxiety, grief, and depression in coastal communities.

noticias.titulo: South Sudan: UN mission decries deadly attacks, works to calm tensions after ‘nothing but devastation’
noticias.resumen: The UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) has condemned recent armed group attacks in Warrap state which reportedly left more than 60 civilians dead and 50 others injured.

noticias.titulo: World marks second warmest July on record
noticias.resumen: As multiple regions contend with unbearable heat, drought, wildfires and other extreme weather, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) on Tuesday underlined the crucial need for stronger forecasts and early warning systems to protect lives and livelihoods.

noticias.titulo: Security Council LIVE: Spotlight on Israeli settler violence in West Bank
noticias.resumen: The Security Council held an open debate on Tuesday which is expected to address escalating Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank as attacks on Palestinians and their property continue. UN News app users can follow here.

noticias.titulo: El calor de los océanos alcanzó un máximo histórico en julio en medio de múltiples extremos climáticos
noticias.resumen: La Organización Meteorológica Mundial explica que el calentamiento global provocado por el cambio climático está intensificando los episodios de calor extremo.

noticias.titulo: Colombia: agua potable, atención médica y alimentos, entre las necesidades urgentes tras el terremoto
noticias.resumen: Las réplicas continúan representando un riesgo para pacientes, trabajadores sanitarios e infraestructuras críticas. Equipos de salud de Naciones Unidas ya se encuentran en Cali y el departamento del Chocó, mientras se evalúan los daños y las necesidades en las zonas más afectadas.

noticias.titulo: After post-pandemic improvement, youth unemployment is rising again
noticias.resumen: Frustrated by skyrocketing youth unemployment, among other issues, tens of thousands of Gen Z activists took to the streets of Nepal last year, demanding a stake in the country’s economic growth. The protest worked and the prime minister resigned.

noticias.titulo: Ebola deaths top 2,000 as scientists race to develop vaccine
noticias.resumen: Local officials in the DR Congo (DRC) reported on Tuesday that deaths from the Ebola virus disease have surpassed 2,000, with half of that number in the last 20 days.

noticias.titulo: Colombia earthquake: UN joins national response
noticias.resumen: As earthquake rescue efforts across western Colombia continued on Tuesday, UN agencies said that they stood ready to help “with everything we've got”, in coordination with national authorities.

noticias.titulo: Myanmar: UN investigators document deliberate military attacks on civilians
noticias.resumen: Myanmar's military has carried out a sustained campaign of deliberate attacks on civilians – including airstrikes on homes, schools and camps for displaced people, alongside arbitrary detention, torture and sexual violence – according to Human Rights Council-appointed investigators.

noticias.titulo: Documentan ataques deliberados contra civiles, escuelas y hospitales en Myanmar
noticias.resumen: Detrás de cada fotografía, testimonio o imagen satelital hay comunidades que viven bajo la amenaza constante de la violencia. Miembros de la entidad encargada de investigar los crímenes en Myanmar están preservando esas pruebas para que puedan utilizarse en futuros procesos judiciales y determinar quiénes ordenaron y ejecutaron los crímenes más graves.

noticias.titulo: Colombia: La ONU reorienta recursos y despliega personal para apoyar la respuesta al terremoto
noticias.resumen: El Gobierno colombiano pidió a Naciones Unidas complementar la respuesta nacional. La Organización ya moviliza suministros y personal hacia las zonas afectadas, mientras advierte que todavía se desconoce el impacto real en comunidades rurales y remotas.

noticias.titulo: "No son incidentes aislados": las políticas israelíes en Cisjordania son pasos coordinados hacia la anexión
noticias.resumen: El coordinador adjunto para el Proceso de Paz en Oriente Medio advierte ante el Consejo de Seguridad que la Cisjordania ocupada ha llegado a un "punto de quiebre" debido a la violencia sin precedentes de los colonos y la rápida expansión de los asentamientos.

noticias.titulo: King Harold may have lost England by backing the wrong pope
noticias.resumen: A forgotten fragment of a lost papal letter is offering a surprising new explanation for the Norman Conquest. England may have backed the wrong pope during a bitter religious power struggle, giving Pope Alexander II a political reason to support William the Conqueror’s invasion. The discovery suggests Harold’s downfall in 1066 was shaped by intrigue in Rome as well as bloodshed at Hastings.

noticias.titulo: Quién era el rapero Tupac Shakur, cómo fue asesinado y por qué 30 años después el crimen sigue sin esclarecerse
noticias.resumen: Han pasado tres décadas desde la muerte de Tupac, y desde entonces, su figura no ha hecho más que crecer.

noticias.titulo: Drought, water rationing and dry rivers: our water crisis is here | Peter Gleick
noticias.resumen: It doesn’t have to be this way. We know what needs to be done Disturbing news about our water resources is now constant and unrelenting. In just the past few weeks, media have reported that Puerto Rico is suffering a deep water crisis as severe drought has cut water supplies to thousands. The Rhine and Po rivers in Europe are at record low levels . The seven states sharing the Colorado River in the US are fighting over unprecedented shortages , while its major reservoirs have shrunk to their lowest levels since they were built. Hungary’s only nuclear power plant is on the verge of shutting…

noticias.titulo: Syrian court sentences Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia for war crimes
noticias.resumen: Verdict relates to atrocities committed during the country’s 14-year civil war in which about 500,000 people died A Syrian court has sentenced the country’s former president Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia for crimes against humanity and war crimes during the 14-year civil war, in which about half a million people died. The two men fled to Moscow after being ousted by a lightning rebel offensive in December 2024 which toppled the dictatorial regime in just 11 days . Continue reading...

noticias.titulo: Black holes older than the Big Bang could explain dark matter
noticias.resumen: Some black holes roaming the Universe today may actually be older than the Big Bang. A new cosmic “bounce” model suggests the Universe expanded from an earlier contracting phase, allowing ancient black holes to survive the transition as cosmic fossils. These relics could potentially explain dark matter and why surprisingly massive objects appeared so early in cosmic history.

noticias.titulo: Scores dead in Colombia after powerful earthquake strikes west of country
noticias.resumen: Quake of 7.4 magnitude collapses and severely damages buildings in several major cities, including Cali and Pereira More than 100 people died after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, collapsing and severely damaging scores of buildings in major cities including Cali and Pereira. The US and Colombian geological surveys reported that a 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck at 7.34am local time on Monday, with its epicentre in the western department of Chocó. It was felt in neighbouring Venezuela, still reeling from a deadly double earthquake on 24 June. Continue reading...
noticias.autor: Tom Phillips, and Thomas Graham in Bogotá

noticias.titulo: The return of the caspian tiger: how a species feared extinct has come back to Kazakhstan
noticias.resumen: The wild capture and release of a female big cat into a nature reserve is the first step towards reintroducing a population that hasn’t been seen for 70 years On 31 July, “Umit” – which means hope in Kazakh – was released into a nature reserve on the edge of Lake Balkhash after more than a decade of careful planning to return the caspian tiger to the region. With this release, Kazakhstan became the first country to restore its tiger range after they had been thought extinct, with the last reliable sighting in the country recorded more than 70 years ago. Umit – a wild-caught female tiger…

noticias.titulo: Quién es Daniel Kinahan, el hombre al que Irlanda acusa de ser el líder de uno de los carteles más peligrosos del mundo
noticias.resumen: El hombre, de 49 años, es señalado por las autoridades como el líder de una organización criminal que mueve más de mil millones de dólares.

noticias.titulo: 'I paid £400 for a Prada bag on Vinted - only to find it was fake'
noticias.resumen: A woman who paid £400 for a Prada handbag on Vinted later discovered it was a fake.

noticias.resumen: Trump Media expects the controversial service, which launched this month, to provide a new revenue stream, as it posts a quarterly loss.

noticias.titulo: Dust and water spotted close to giant black hole
noticias.resumen: Using the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope , an international team of astronomers have discovered that dust and water can form and survive surprisingly close to the supermassive black hole at the centre of our Milky Way galaxy. The observations reveal that the evolved star IRS 3 continues to enrich its surroundings with newly formed material despite the intense radiation environment around Sagittarius A*.

noticias.titulo: Trump explains secret plane switch over possible threat
noticias.resumen: Donald Trump has confirmed US media reports he secretly left Turkey by switching planes via a catering container over a threat from Iran.

noticias.resumen: Now on its 167th edition, the Royal Photographic Society’s annual show features moving explorations of kinks, visual disorders … and long-snouted clowns Continue reading...

Continue reading...
noticias.autor: Adam Fulton, Lucy Campbell, Angus Thomson and Tom Ambrose

noticias.titulo: 150-million-year-old dinosaur footprints reveal something strange about its walk
noticias.resumen: A spectacular 150-million-year-old trail of more than 130 footprints captures a giant sauropod making a complete loop before continuing on its way. Its uneven stride hints that the long-necked dinosaur may have been walking with a limp.

noticias.titulo: La planta de SAIC en Galicia siembra dudas sobre la apuesta estratégica de China por España
noticias.resumen: La compañía china "entiende" que se evalúen todos los factores relevantes para la instalación de la fábrica de MG en Ferrol, incluyendo los de la defensa estratégica de España, y garantiza que "salvaguardará íntegramente" la seguridad nacional. Leer

noticias.titulo: NASA’s moon base is taking shape with 20+ lunar landings planned
noticias.resumen: NASA is assembling the foundations of a future Moon Base through a wave of robotic missions and powerful new commercial landers. More than 20 landings are planned through 2029, testing everything from precision landings and lunar communications to rovers, power systems, and technology that can survive the Moon’s extreme conditions. Upcoming missions could also make history by exploring the Moon’s far side and a mysterious magnetic lunar swirl. Each landing brings NASA closer to a sustained human presence on the lunar surface.

noticias.titulo: A simple blood test could detect multiple cancers and reveal where they started
noticias.resumen: UCLA researchers have created a blood test that can scan DNA signals for multiple cancers, liver diseases, and signs of organ damage—and even indicate where trouble may be developing. Early results suggest the inexpensive approach could bring medicine closer to a single blood test capable of catching a wide range of diseases before they become harder to treat.

noticias.titulo: The secret hidden in these ancient manuscripts isn’t written in ink
noticias.resumen: Researchers can now recover DNA from centuries-old parchment without damaging the manuscripts, turning historic documents into unexpected genetic time capsules. The hidden clues could reveal ancient trade routes, livestock history, manuscript origins, and details of everyday life stretching back more than a thousand years.

noticias.titulo: Exercise may help the aging brain “take out the trash”
noticias.resumen: Regular exercise may help the brain clear away harmful waste that can build up with age. Researchers found that physical activity supports several processes linked to the brain’s glymphatic cleanup system, including better sleep, lower inflammation, and healthier blood vessels. Because this waste-removal system becomes increasingly important as we get older, exercise could play a meaningful role in protecting against cognitive decline.

noticias.titulo: 'I started in my 20s and made £8,000': Why women are often better investors than men
noticias.resumen: Women can make higher returns but only about a quarter of UK women have investments, compared with about 40% of men.

noticias.titulo: Trump recupera su cruzada contra las vacunas y exige reducir las dosis para los niños
noticias.resumen: El presidente de Estados Unidos aprueba una orden ejecutiva que insta a los Estados a revisar sus protocolos sobre las vacunas y separar las dosis en varias citas

noticias.titulo: Italia y Dinamarca piden más deportaciones ante una "inmigración descontrolada"
noticias.resumen: Giorgia Meloni y Mette Frederiksen se alían para exigir en la UE una política estricta frente a la inmigración ilegal, a la que vinculan con el aumento de la criminalidad y de la violencia sexual. Leer

noticias.titulo: Police use teargas on young Indians as government jobs protest escalates
noticias.resumen: Demonstrators accuse authorities of failing to tackle irregularities in exams for sought-after civil service jobs Thousands of angry young job-seekers clashed with police in Jharkhand, one of India’s poorest states, on Monday as a weeks-long protest over alleged irregularities in recruitment drives for coveted government jobs escalated into a march on the state legislature. Police fired water cannon and teargas and swung batons as they tried to stop flag-waving demonstrators from clambering over barricades and surging towards the assembly in Ranchi, the state capital. Some of the protesters…

noticias.titulo: New GLP-1 pill delivers up to 12% weight loss in 36 weeks
noticias.resumen: An experimental GLP-1 pill helped people with obesity or overweight lose as much as 12.1% of their body weight in just 36 weeks. Unlike injectable drugs such as Wegovy and Ozempic, aleniglipron is a small molecule that can be taken once daily with or without food and could potentially be produced more easily at scale.

noticias.titulo: Lion Nebula roars to life for Webb
noticias.resumen: Image: Observing across the starry 'plains' of space, the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope has taken images of NGC 2392, nicknamed the Lion Nebula. The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope previously viewed this planetary nebula in 2000, imaging the lion face-shaped target in visible light and revealing features such as the “mane” of hazy, comet-shaped objects. Now Webb has captured a clearer, more detailed view of the Lion Nebula due to its high-resolution imaging. At first glance the nebula’s overall structure in Webb’s infrared images, both with the NIRCam (Near Infrared Camera) and MIR…

noticias.titulo: 1 in 5 people may carry this hidden genetic heart risk
noticias.resumen: Very high levels of the inherited cholesterol-related particle Lp(a) were linked to a greater risk of major cardiovascular events, particularly stroke and cardiovascular death, in a study of more than 20,000 people. Since elevated Lp(a) often flies completely under the radar, a simple blood test could uncover hidden heart risk that standard cholesterol testing may miss.

noticias.titulo: Wildfires, drought and extreme heat, 2026
noticias.resumen: Earth observation satellites help us monitor phenomena such as wildfires, drought and heatwaves from space. This page is updated on a regular basis with a selection of ESA’s most recent news-related images showing how the effects of climate change are impacting our world.

noticias.titulo: Meta to open source its most powerful AI model as it takes swipe at OpenAI, Anthropic
noticias.resumen: Meta launched Muse Glimmer and plans to release Muse Spark 1.2 weights as Zuckerberg pushes for U.S. leadership in open AI.

noticias.titulo: Scientists discover a hidden switch inside silver nanocatalysts
noticias.resumen: Silver nanocatalysts have been found to switch where they perform their most important reactions depending on whether a solid oxide cell is making electricity or hydrogen. The discovery could enable smarter catalyst designs that boost clean power generation while making green hydrogen more energy-efficient.

noticias.titulo: La ONU ofrece apoyo a Colombia tras el terremoto de magnitud 7,4 que dejó más de 100 muertos
noticias.resumen: El sistema de Naciones Unidas sigue de cerca la emergencia y está preparado para apoyar la respuesta nacional. El potente sismo golpeó el oeste del país, provocó derrumbes y dejó personas atrapadas, mientras las autoridades continúan evaluando los daños y el número de víctimas.

noticias.titulo: Fighting deepens needs and fuels further displacement in Sudan
noticias.resumen: Ongoing conflict, displacement and funding shortages continue to deepen needs in Sudan, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warned on Monday, underscoring the need for greater civilian protection.

noticias.titulo: Lebanon: UN peacekeepers count hundreds of Israeli strikes and incursions in a single weekend
noticias.resumen: Israeli forces fired 455 projectiles into south Lebanon and breached Lebanese airspace 97 times between Friday and Sunday, the UN's peacekeeping mission in the country reported Monday – among the heaviest fire seen in months.

noticias.titulo: UN offers support to Colombia after magnitude 7.4 earthquake kills dozens
noticias.resumen: The UN offered its support to Colombia on Monday after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck the west of the country, killing at least 111 people and injuring at least 87, including several children, while leaving others trapped under the rubble and causing landslides and serious damage to homes and infrastructure.

noticias.titulo: DR Congo: Ebola is killing people before they ever reach a doctor
noticias.resumen: More than 1,900 people have died in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak – and most of them never made it to a treatment centre. Between 60 and 70 per cent of deaths are happening in communities far from care, a gap that is now central to the World Health Organization's response.

noticias.titulo: Afghanistan: UN tells Taliban to open up on abuses committed by security forces
noticias.resumen: Five years into Taliban rule, Afghans still have almost no way of knowing whether soldiers, police and morality officers who abuse their power ever face consequences – and that secrecy is corroding trust in the State, the UN said Monday.

noticias.titulo: UN calls for urgent action to protect children from online information risks
noticias.resumen: More than eight in 10 young people aged 15 to 24 worldwide are now online, and in low-income countries they outpace the rest of the population nearly two to one.

noticias.titulo: Humanitarian aid warehouses come under attack in Ukraine
noticias.resumen: Russia’s ongoing full-scale invasion of Ukraine has left civilians vulnerable to repeated deadly attacks and humanitarian workers and key facilities being targeted and destroyed.

noticias.titulo: Expertos condenan la escalada de ataques contra palestinos en Gaza y Cisjordania
noticias.resumen: Un grupo de expertos en derechos humanos alertan del agudo deterioro de la situación en Palestina: 160 muertos en Gaza en julio y terror de colonos en Cisjordania. Denuncian que el genocidio continúa, la ayuda alimentaria no llega y las restricciones de movimiento son "instrumentos letales" que han costado la vida a un bebé y una mujer embarazada.

noticias.titulo: Equipos para elaborar productos cotidianos pueden terminar en la fabricación de drogas
noticias.resumen: Prensas para tabletas, reactores, mezcladoras y equipos de laboratorio tienen numerosos usos legítimos, pero también pueden terminar en instalaciones clandestinas. Un nuevo análisis identifica los puntos de la cadena comercial donde existe mayor riesgo de desvío.

noticias.titulo: Rusia destruye un almacén con suministros médicos en Ucrania
noticias.resumen: La agencia de salud logró trasladar parte de los suministros antes de que el edificio fuera destruido por completo. Los suministros estaban destinados a apoyar la atención médica de emergencia y mantener servicios esenciales en instalaciones sanitarias próximas a las zonas de combate.

noticias.titulo: Casi ningún país avanza al ritmo necesario para transformar sus sistemas alimentarios
noticias.resumen: La transformación de los sistemas alimentarios no depende solo de producir más comida. También exige dietas saludables, menor contaminación, mejores condiciones para quienes trabajan en el sector, instituciones más eficaces y una mayor capacidad para resistir crisis económicas y climáticas.

noticias.titulo: 240-million-year-old reptile fossil reveals a lost chapter before dinosaurs and crocodiles
noticias.resumen: A 240-million-year-old reptile discovered in Brazil is revealing what evolution looked like just before the rise of dinosaurs and crocodiles. The small predator had unusually positioned legs that may have allowed it to move more efficiently than many earlier reptiles. Its close relatives were previously known mostly from other continents, suggesting these ancient animals spread much farther across the Triassic world than scientists realized.

noticias.titulo: Potatoes may have given Indigenous Andeans a digestive superpower
noticias.resumen: The rise of the potato in the Andes appears to have left a lasting mark on human DNA. Indigenous Peruvians carry exceptionally high numbers of a starch-digestion gene, likely because people with more copies gained an evolutionary advantage once potatoes became a staple food. The change began thousands of years before European contact, providing unusually strong evidence that diet can shape human evolution.

noticias.titulo: Invisible poison: living with mercury pollution in the Colombian Amazon – in pictures
noticias.resumen: Rainforest communities face a silent crisis as mercury from gold mining contaminates their food and water Continue reading...
noticias.autor: Luis Bernardo Cano in Leticia, Colombia

noticias.titulo: Todos necesitan a Trump: cómo EE.UU. tutela los intereses opuestos de gobierno y oposición en Venezuela
noticias.resumen: La creciente influencia de Washington sobre lo que ocurre en Caracas es palpable no solamente en las acciones y decisiones del gobierno de Delcy Rodríguez, sino también en las acciones y silencios de la oposición.

noticias.titulo: The sun will vanish over Europe in a rare total solar eclipse: Watch live
noticias.resumen: A total solar eclipse will plunge parts of Europe into darkness on August 12, 2026, with Spain offering some of the best views. ESA will livestream the spectacle from the Javalambre Observatory, combining telescope feeds, drone footage, and expert commentary. At 20:31 CEST, the observatory will experience 1 minute and 21 seconds of totality, revealing the Sun’s normally hidden outer atmosphere.

noticias.titulo: El Gobierno puede poner condiciones a SAIC en Galicia para garantizar la seguridad nacional
noticias.resumen: Óscar López niega que vaya a rechazarse esta inversión, que requiere la aprobación del Consejo de Ministros, por motivos de seguridad y dice que se están analizando todas las "implicaciones" que conlleva para tomar "las decisiones oportunas". Leer

noticias.titulo: Voyager 2 was running out of power. NASA just bought it more time
noticias.resumen: NASA engineers have found a clever way to squeeze more life out of Voyager 2, nearly half a century after it left Earth. In an operation nicknamed the “Big Bang,” the team simultaneously shut down certain power-hungry hardware and switched to lower-power alternatives while keeping the spacecraft warm enough to survive.

noticias.titulo: Teletrabajar con aire acondicionado puede disparar la factura de la luz hasta más de 60 euros al mes
noticias.resumen: Utilizar el aire acondicionado ocho horas al día durante todo el mes puede añadir entre 18,43 y 61,44 euros mensuales a la factura eléctrica, según Leer

noticias.titulo: El negocio 'kidult' alcanza los 1.200 millones en España y prevé un crecimiento del 5% hasta 2030
noticias.resumen: Más de la mitad de los ingresos del sector corresponde a juguetes, coleccionables y videojuegos para adultos. Leer

noticias.titulo: An indigenous photographic history of America – in pictures
noticias.resumen: Spanning generations and multiple Indigenous societies and nations, In Light and Shadow traces the visual importance of Indigenous photographers. Representing work in different genres, the book presents more than 250 images with an accompanying exhibition at Obscura Gallery from 14 August Continue reading...

noticias.titulo: For 15,000 years, humans and dogs have been changing each other
noticias.resumen: Dogs have been shaping—and being shaped by—humans for about 15,000 years, evolving from early partners of hunter-gatherers into an astonishing range of specialized companions. Across the globe, they adapted alongside people to wildly different environments and needs, from powerful Arctic sled dogs and agile rainforest hunters to high-altitude dogs with genetic traits for surviving thin air. Some were even bred for wool, while others played important spiritual or ceremonial roles.

noticias.titulo: Cassini reveals a surprising twist in Saturn’s magnetic shield
noticias.resumen: Cassini data has revealed a surprising twist in Saturn’s magnetic shield: the planet’s rapid rotation appears to drag a key opening in its magnetosphere far toward the afternoon side instead of keeping it near noon, as happens on Earth. The finding confirms that giant planets like Saturn operate under a fundamentally different magnetic regime, where fast spin and charged material from moons such as Enceladus can overpower the Sun’s influence.
